prompt.context_jp: 夏の終わり___近づく頃、高野誠一の古い一軒家には、相変わらずのんびりとした空気が漂っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夏の終わり___近づく頃…

feedback.correct_en: The subordinate clause describes a new, scene-setting event (the end of summer approaching). New-information subjects inside relative/temporal clauses take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would promote 'end of summer' to the main topic, which clashes with the subordinate 頃 clause. を doesn't fit an intransitive verb like 近づく.

prompt.context_jp: この家に同居する雨宮蛍___、長い空白を経て、ようやく恋を手に入れたばかりである。
prompt.prompt_jp: 雨宮蛍___、長い空白を経て…

feedback.correct_en: Hotaru is being introduced as the topic of this whole descriptive sentence about her situation. は marks her as the theme the narrator then comments on.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal brand-new identification, but here the narrator is framing a known character for commentary. に doesn't fit the grammatical role.

contrast_examples.en: As for Hotaru, she found love.
It was Hotaru who found love.

prompt.context_jp: 同じ頃、居間では高野___ひとり、腕を組んで立ち尽くしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 居間では高野___ひとり…

feedback.correct_en: The sentence introduces Takano as the newly-focused figure in a new scene ('meanwhile in the living room…'). New-information subjects in scene-setting narration take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would reframe Takano as the running topic, but the location では already carries the topic role here. も would wrongly imply 'also'.

contrast_examples.jp: 居間では高野が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: In the living room, Takano was standing (new scene).

contrast_examples.jp: 高野は居間で立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: Takano (topic) was standing in the living room.

prompt.context_jp: 「なぜ 彼___ できたのに 君は変わらない？」
prompt.prompt_jp: なぜ 彼___ できたのに…

feedback.correct_en: 彼ができる ('to get a boyfriend') is a fixed existential pattern that takes が — it reports the appearance of something new.
feedback.incorrect_en: 彼はできた would mean 'as for a boyfriend, (something) was completed' — it loses the 'got a boyfriend' meaning. に doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: We had a child (one came into being).

prompt.context_jp: 家での干物ぶりとは打って変わって、会社での蛍___それなりにきちんとした社員の顔をしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 会社での蛍___きちんとした社員の顔をしていた。

feedback.correct_en: The sentence explicitly contrasts home-Hotaru vs. office-Hotaru (家での…とは打って変わって). Contrastive は marks the office version against the home version.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce her as new information, losing the contrast setup. も ('also') contradicts the opposition.

contrast_examples.jp: 家ではだらしないが、会社ではきちんとしている。
contrast_examples.en: Sloppy at home, but proper at work.

contrast_examples.jp: 蛍がきちんとしている。

prompt.context_jp: 蛍の視線___、自然とガラス張りのミーティングルームへ吸い寄せられていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛍の視線___、ミーティングルームへ吸い寄せられていた。

feedback.correct_en: 蛍の視線 is already an established element (we know she's watching). は presents it as the topic of the comment that follows.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight 視線 as new information, which doesn't fit the ongoing scene. を doesn't match the passive 吸い寄せられる.

contrast_examples.jp: 視線は窓の外に向いた。
contrast_examples.en: Her gaze turned outside the window.

prompt.context_jp: 「私は元気ですよ 大丈夫です｡ 恋愛だけ___ すべてじゃないですから｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 恋愛だけ___ すべてじゃない

feedback.correct_en: The 〜だけが〜ではない pattern is a fixed exhaustive-listing construction meaning 'it's not only X that…'. が is required here.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would mean 'at least love', giving the opposite emphasis. だけも is ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.jp: 金だけがすべてじゃない。

contrast_examples.en: Let me at least say this.

prompt.context_jp: 「自分の家に なかなか彼女を呼ばないの___ 彼女に対しての本気度が低め｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: …呼ばないの___ 本気度が低め。

feedback.correct_en: The 〜のは〜 cleft pattern sets up a topic ('the fact that he doesn't invite her') and comments on it. は is the fixed choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would turn it into an identificational 'what is low is…' structure that doesn't match the predicate. を doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.jp: 呼ばないのは本気じゃない証拠。
contrast_examples.en: Not inviting her is proof he's not serious.
What's sad is that he doesn't invite her.

prompt.context_jp: マコトが自分の席へ戻っていったあとも、蛍___しばらくその場から動けなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛍___しばらくその場から動けなかった。

feedback.correct_en: Hotaru is the running topic of this scene. は continues the narrative focus on her reaction after Makoto leaves.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would wrongly treat her as new information after she's been the center of the scene for several sentences.

prompt.context_jp: けれども、顔___熱くなっていくのだけは、どうにも止められない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 顔___熱くなっていく…

feedback.correct_en: Inside the のだけは nominalized clause, the subject 顔 is new information describing a physical sensation. Embedded subjects of 〜なる typically take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this noun clause would wrongly add a second topic layer. を doesn't fit the intransitive 熱くなる.

prompt.context_jp: 「うん 元カノのため___買ったやつなら｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 元カノのため___買ったやつ

feedback.correct_en: ために ('for the sake of') attaches with に to mark purpose/beneficiary. The toothbrush was bought for the ex-girlfriend's sake.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks means/location, not beneficiary. を would make 'ex-girlfriend's sake' a direct object, which is nonsensical.

contrast_examples.en: I bought it at the station.

prompt.context_jp: 「やっぱりだ｡ 一緒に暮らしてるんだな｡ 手嶋___ かわいそうだな｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 手嶋___ かわいそうだな

feedback.correct_en: Futatsuki is piling pity on Teshima in addition to the unfolding mess — も ('also/even') captures that extension. Source text uses も here.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just identify the pitiable person neutrally, losing the 'on top of everything else' flavor. を doesn't fit an adjective predicate.

prompt.context_jp: 「優華には 優華の魅力___あるんだから｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 優華の魅力___あるんだから

feedback.correct_en: ある ('there is') takes が for its existing subject. Yamada is asserting that Yuka's own charm exists.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would introduce contrast ('as for Yuka's charm, it exists… but'), which is not Yamada's point. を doesn't go with ある.

prompt.context_jp: 「部長___ いい体してますよね｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 部長___ いい体してますよね

feedback.correct_en: The source uses って, the casual topic marker equivalent to は, to flag 部長 as the theme of her observation. It fits the chatty tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly identify the manager as new info in a flattering comment. を doesn't fit the predicate してる.

contrast_examples.jp: 部長っていい人ですよね。
contrast_examples.en: The manager's a good person, right?

prompt.context_jp: 「体脂肪率___！ 私の体脂肪率が 13％しか ありません！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 体脂肪率___！

feedback.correct_en: Hotaru is exclaiming a surprising new fact about the number. が marks the subject of the sudden discovery.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a calm topic statement, losing the shock. を doesn't fit an existential predicate.

prompt.context_jp: 「恋は 女___美しくするんですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 恋は 女___美しくする

feedback.correct_en: 美しくする is a transitive causative ('make X beautiful'). 女 is its direct object, marked by を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 女 the subject, flipping the sentence into 'women make (something) beautiful'. に doesn't match this verb.

prompt.context_jp: 蛍は鞄を下ろしながら、ついマコトの席のほうへ目を___。
prompt.prompt_jp: マコトの席のほうへ目を___

feedback.correct_en: 目をやる is a set collocation meaning 'to glance/cast one's eyes toward'. It captures the involuntary, quick look.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目を見た would mean 'looked at (someone's) eyes'. 目を置く isn't an idiom here.

contrast_examples.en: To look into the other person's eyes.

prompt.context_jp: 蛍は机の下で、___拳を握りしめた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___拳を握りしめた
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the mimetic word that fits.

feedback.correct_en: ぎゅっと expresses tight clenching — the right intensity for a nervous, resolute gesture under the desk.
feedback.incorrect_en: ふわっと means 'softly/fluffily' — the opposite of clenching. さらっと means 'smoothly/casually'.

prompt.context_jp: 「他にあるだろ？ ずっと1人 胸の___ しまい込んでたこと｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 胸の___しまい込んでたこと

feedback.correct_en: 胸の奥にしまう ('to keep locked in the depths of one's heart') is a fixed emotional idiom for hidden feelings.
feedback.incorrect_en: 胸の下 (literally 'under the chest') is anatomical, not emotional. 胸の前 means physically 'in front of the chest'.

contrast_examples.jp: 秘密を胸の奥にしまう。
contrast_examples.en: Keep a secret deep in one's heart.
Fold hands in front of the chest.

prompt.context_jp: 「3週間目に フンコロガシに いってやったわ｡ ｢幸せになってね｣って｡ 笑顔で___宣言よ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 笑顔で___宣言よ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that fits Yamada's story.

feedback.correct_en: Yamada lost the romantic rivalry and said goodbye with a smile — 敗北宣言 ('declaration of defeat') is exactly what she describes.
feedback.incorrect_en: 勝利宣言 ('victory declaration') is the opposite. 独立宣言 ('declaration of independence') doesn't fit a love-triangle context.

prompt.context_jp: 「本当は 男の胸___ 借りると いいんだけどねぇ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 男の胸___ 借りる

feedback.correct_en: 胸を借りる ('to borrow someone's chest/shoulder to cry on') is a fixed idiom; the chest is the direct object marked by を.
feedback.incorrect_en: 胸が借りる would make 'the chest' the borrower, which is nonsensical. 胸に borrows something to the chest, not the idiom.

contrast_examples.en: Put a hand on one's chest.

prompt.context_jp: 「クライアントから クレーム来たの 処理お願い｡ 2年前の依頼主よ 菓子折り持って 頭___来て｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 頭___来て
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for the apology idiom.

feedback.correct_en: 頭を下げる ('bow one's head') is the standard idiom for apologizing. Yamada is sending Hotaru to apologize.
feedback.incorrect_en: 頭を上げる means to raise one's head — the opposite of apologizing. 頭を振る means to shake one's head (refuse).

prompt.context_jp: 「申し訳ございません！ 心より ___申し上げます！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 心より ___申し上げます

feedback.correct_en: お詫び申し上げます is the formal, business-grade apology phrase. Hotaru is handling a client complaint and uses the highest register.
feedback.incorrect_en: ごめん申し上げます is ungrammatical — ごめん is casual. 謝り申し上げます is not a standard set phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: 深くお詫び申し上げます。

prompt.context_jp: 彼女の額に指先で___！って言わせてやりたい衝動を、高野はどうにか飲み込んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 指先で___!
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the mimetic word fitting a finger-tap.

feedback.correct_en: コツン is the sharp, light sound of tapping something hard with a fingertip — exactly a flick to the forehead.
feedback.incorrect_en: ゴロゴロ suggests rolling or thundering. ふわふわ is fluffy/soft.

prompt.context_jp: Hotaru backs out of sleeping over, inventing a cold.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Hotaru's awkward retreat?

choices.text: 風邪の ひき始めかも｡ うつすと悪いから 帰ります｡
風邪の 開始かも｡ 伝染すると悪いから 帰宅します｡
風邪を始めるかも｡ うつしたら悪いから 帰らせていただく｡

feedback.correct_en: The source uses ひき始め (natural collocation for catching a cold) and うつす ('pass on' an illness) — everyday register perfect for this apologetic retreat.
feedback.incorrect_en: 開始/伝染/帰宅 are overly stiff and clinical. 風邪を始める is not a natural collocation — you don't 'start' a cold.

contrast_examples.en: Pass on a cold to someone.

prompt.context_jp: Hotaru collapses on the engawa with a beer after a brutal workday.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for her sigh of relief?

choices.text: あ～！ やっぱ 家が一番！
ああ！ やはり 家屋が最良である！
あ～！ 家は 一番やっぱり！

feedback.correct_en: やっぱ家が一番 is the natural, casual exclamation — the colloquial contraction of やっぱり and the standard 〜が一番 pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: 家屋/最良/である is literary/formal and clashes with her relaxed porch moment. Option c scrambles the word order unnaturally.

contrast_examples.jp: やはり家屋が最良である。

prompt.context_jp: Futatsuki is giving Takano blunt advice over the phone.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as Futatsuki's directive?

choices.text: 一緒に暮らすのは やめろ｡
一緒に暮らすこと お停止してください｡
一緒 暮らしを やめるんだぞ｡

feedback.correct_en: 〜のはやめろ is a natural blunt imperative between male friends. It matches Futatsuki's exasperated, direct tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: お停止してください mixes polite prefix with an unnatural stiff verb. Option c garbles the nominal phrase and ends awkwardly.

contrast_examples.jp: ご使用をおやめください。

prompt.context_jp: Hotaru responds to Yuka's declaration of defeat.

choices.text: 幸福を取得してください｡

feedback.correct_en: 幸せになってね is the warm, standard farewell blessing — exactly echoing Yamada's earlier 'declaration of defeat' story.
feedback.incorrect_en: 幸福を取得する sounds like bureaucratic 'acquire happiness'. 幸せに変化する ('transform into happiness') is unidiomatic.

prompt.context_jp: Takano snaps at Hotaru's lazy jogging plan.
prompt.prompt_en: Which scolding line sounds most natural?

choices.text: 甘えたこと いってるな！ 24時間 走って来い！
甘え事を 言っていらっしゃるな！ 24時間ご走行ください！
甘ったれるな いってるんだ！ 24時間 走られて来い！

feedback.correct_en: The source line uses the blunt imperative 走って来い and the natural 〜ことをいってるな scolding pattern — fitting Takano's boss-at-home voice.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b mixes keigo prefixes with scolding, which is incoherent. Option c has a mangled verbal structure (走られて来い) that isn't used.
